The contents slide lists sections 7. Ignition and 8. Service; the transcript states that Ignition and services will be covered.
Architecture overview showing OptiSweep modules, UPS equipment, PLCs, Ignition, Aveva HMI, SQL Server, and Geek+ integration.
The XLe chat OBC communication module subscribes to tags in Ignition and allows reading and writing from the tippers; XLe chat is used for secure communication through an S tunnel.
The Sorter Sweeper module is a tote state machine that tracks incoming packages, updates information, tracks totes at the tipper, and requests tote actions from the Robotics module.
The Robotics module handles tote movement requests through maps; the Geek+ comm module translates commands for Geek+ and sends them as API requests.
Ignition is the HMI base used to collect data and send it to Aveva for UPS; the diagram includes an Ignition OPC server and Aveva HMI.
The Sorter Sweeper module orchestrates tote movement and functions as the state machine for totes.
The Sorter Robotics module acts as the state machine for AGVs, receives tote tasks from Sorter Sweeper, and generates commands for Geek Plus.
OPC COM subscribes to OPC tags, sends updates to Sorter Sweeper, and writes Sorter Sweeper data to the OPC server.
XLE COM manages communication between Sorter Sweeper and the UPS Chat server; exchanged data includes tote, scan, sort, destination, close, and print-label messages.
The source describes scan dimensions, load category, possible destinations, sort confirmation, hot bin messages, Sure Post notification, destination closure, and print-label data.
Training video slide labeled "Database Walkthrough" at 00:07:52.000–00:07:56.000.
The Robotics module acts as the state machine for AGVs and receives tote tasks from the SorterSweeper module.
The slide lists AGV commands including induct tote, remove tote, pickup tote, move tote, drop off tote, cancel request, and go charge.
The Robotics module generates commands for Geek+ to execute AGV tote tasks; the design diagram includes a Geek+ Comm Module.
The speaker introduces a walkthrough of all the tables; the slide displays “Database Walkthrough.”
The transcript says the presenter will walk through “all the tables.”
Slide frame captured at 00:08:52.500; OCR reads “Database Walkthrough.”
The WCS includes data containers, entity logs, and PLC communication; OptiSweep uses several related databases and SQL Jobs for cleanup.
OptiSweep only utilizes EntityLogs for logging; the logged information includes code location and error-related fields useful for debugging.
Audit tracks the AGDID, current Geek task ID, and robotics command GUID; Geek AGV action logging records tasks sent to Geek Plus.
The lattice code model maps station IDs to lattice codes used by Geek for tote induction and drop-off locations.
OPC configuration stores connection parameters, while OPC tags stores tags subscribed to at startup and used for reading and writing.
The Robot Location database model contains information about station number, occupancy, zone, closeout zone, location type, maximum AGVs, and dwell-time tracking.
The training lists location types covering sorter, tipper, hospital, shutdown, and GLD queue locations.
The Sorter Side database model defines sorter-side entrance and exit queue locations, tipper count, and disabled state; the slide shows four SorterSide records.
The transcript describes round-robin or closest-tipper selection, traffic balancing, and more even utilization of tippers associated with sorter sides.
The training distinguishes zones, RMS node-code terminology, cell codes, and centimeter-based XY location coordinates.
Training slide labeled "Robotics Database Overview" with visible database model entities.
The Robotics Database overview visibly lists Robot, RobotCommand, RobotCommandActivity, RobotLocation, and RobotTaskActivity entities and associated timing, status, identifier, and location fields.
The slide lists charging, dwell, system-error, task, tote, tipper-station, and sorter-related database entities and fields.
The training explains that sorter sides are mapped to nearby tippers and that the number of tippers can vary by configuration.
The initial CSV configuration populates the database; items outside the active phase are disabled and can be enabled in a later database update.
The sort locations database model contains sorted locations, queue locations behind the sorted locations, associated sorter sides, and entrance-queue sequence.
The shutdown staging table maps AGV locations during shutdown and distinguishes staging for AGVs with totes from staging for AGVs without totes.
The captured training frame shows the robotics database shutdown staging model and tote-status field.
The transcript describes a mapping file that associates sequence values, including sequence four, with sorter stations or locations.
The speaker calls the value a sorter zone exit queue sequence ID and observes that the queue can also be viewed as an array.
The transcript explains that compression keeps AGVs from the same zone together and that the software handles the compression logic.
OCR from the captured RMS Map Monitor screen shows 'Currently in system emergency stop state' and identifies the map monitoring page as an emergency-stop trigger.
The charging database model includes separate tables for charging areas, charging locations, and charging thresholds.
Charging areas store entrance IDs, exit IDs, and whether the area is disabled; each area has several chargers.
Charging location records store individual chargers, their stations, associated tote stands, charging-area associations, and disabled status.
The charging threshold table stores values used in code to determine whether an AGV needs charge, can be released from a charger, or needs emergency charge.
Sorter-side identifiers are model IDs used to associate chargers with sorter sides; assigned chargers are used normally, with another side's available charger described for emergency use.
A captured training frame discusses the sorter-side database model and sorter-side identifiers.
The Robot Command Database model table tracks the status of robot commands requested by the Robotics module for AGVs; completed commands are archived to Robot Command Activity.
Internal generic commands are translated by the Geek Plus COM module into the vendor REST API and converted back to the internal format.
Completed commands are archived into Robot Command Activity, which contains command, robot, container, station, status, parameter, timing, circuit, and total-time information.
The robot database model includes current and destination location information, and robot location data includes maximum AGV capacity for queues or stations.
Because charging control was transferred through the integration, WCS is responsible for assigning AGVs to chargers rather than RMS.
The Robot Task database model table tracks the status of the tote task requested by the Sorter Sweeper module. When tasks are complete, they are archived to Robot Task Activity.
The AGV error model table stores the list of errors, their codes, and a description of the error. For metric purposes, errors are classified as critical or non-critical.
The displayed AGV error example includes an error code and the description 'Front bumper trigger.'
The AGV Active Error Database model table logs AGV active errors currently in the system and includes the name or robot code, error code, description, and Sort GUID.
When an error is resolved or the AGV is removed, the errors are archived to the AGVErrorActivityDatabaseModel.
The Location Active Dwell model table displays active dwells at sort locations marked for dwell tracking. Once the AGV leaves, the activity is archived to Location Dwell Activity.
Dwell time is described as how long an AGV has been sitting at a particular location.
The LocationActiveDwellModel table displays the active dwells at locations marked for DwellTracking; the table includes AgvName, Station, and SortGuid.
Once the AGV leaves, the dwell is complete and the activity is archived to LocationDwellActivity. The displayed fields include AgvName, Station, SortGuid, Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time.
The training discusses dwell information as a way to identify bottlenecks or idle time, including how long an AGV waits at a hospital and how long a tote sits at a tipper before tipping.
The System Error Definition table stores the definition of system errors; the displayed table includes error, area, description, and resolution fields.
The System Active Error model shows any active errors currently in the system and includes the name, area, area code, and description of the error.
Once an active error is resolved, it is archived to the System Error Activity model table; displayed records include description, resolution, start time, finish time, and duration.
The SystemDatabaseModel shows the configuration, state of the system, and current sort GUID.
The current state of the system is stored in the SystemDatabaseModel; listed values include startup, running, shutdown, zone configuration, and closeout states.
The displayed SystemDatabaseModel query includes EntityInserted, EntityLastUpdate, Status, and SortGuid fields.

The Items model represents parcels on the sorter, listens to Scan Data 2, sort, and sort-confirm messages, updates items as messages arrive, and removes them when they divert to their final destination.
Scan Data 2 provides the package unique ID, tracking number, length, width and height, weight, and package classification.
The cube adjustment model uses package classification, the default dimension model supplies dimensions when data is missing, and the displayed cube is based on a squashed or implanted cube.
Missing dimension data becomes true when default dimensions are used and provides a way to count items with missing dimensional information.
Lane activity shows message types, associates packages with auto-induct sources using package ID, and displays sort-confirm zone and lane information together with package dimensions and cube.
The Research destinations model stores destinations for packages that go off the end of the sorter.
A closed chute creates an active exchange; when an empty tote replaces it, the exchange is archived to exchange activity.
Bag-out activity is recorded in active bag out and archived to bag out activity after the tote has been tipped.
OptiSweep listens for GEEK AGV and E-stop callbacks, records E-stop identity and active state, and measures E-stop duration.
The Reset Metrics API opens closed chutes, creates a new SortName and SortGuid, and supports historical sort-to-sort metrics.
The system state model tracks system status, chute-closure behavior after bag-out, sort-data reception, zone configuration, and closeout states.
Tasks sent to the robotics engine are tracked in the task model and completed tasks are archived to task activity.
Database jobs run housekeeping every 12 hours and remove older data to support database memory management; some retention periods were described as approximately three to seven days.

structured_payload.title: Inspect Robot Location Attributes in the Robotics Database
structured_payload.candidate_goal: Use the Robotics database Robot Location model/table to inspect live station and location attributes used by OptiSweep.
structured_payload.summary: A read-only SSMS diagnostic for checking Robot Location records, including station number, occupancy, zone, closeout zone, location type, maximum AGVs, and dwell-time tracking.
rough_steps: Open SSMS and select the OptiSweep Robotics database.
Locate the Robot Location database model/table and inspect the record for the relevant station or location.

Check the station number, occupied state, zone, closeout zone, location type, maximum number of AGVs allowed, and dwell-time tracking field. [Image support needed: Robotics database Robot Location model/table showing these location attributes.]

Compare the live record with the location being investigated in RMS, where the source identifies orange locations and workstation IDs as visible location cues. [Image support needed: RMS map or location view showing orange locations and workstation IDs.]
structured_payload.expected_result: The relevant Robot Location record is present and its live fields are readable: station or location identity, occupied state, zone, closeout zone, location type, maximum-AGV value, and dwell-time tracking setting. The record can be associated with the corresponding RMS location cue.
failure_or_escalation_notes: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the expected Robot Location record is missing, cannot be associated with the RMS location, or contains blank or inconsistent identifying fields.
Do not modify database records as part of this diagnostic.
access_or_tools_needed: RMS / fleet status UI for location comparison

evidence_source_refs.quote_or_summary: The Robot Location database model/table includes station number, occupied state, zone, closeout zone, location type, maximum AGVs allowed, and dwell-time tracking.

structured_payload.title: Diagnose Sorter Location and Queue Mapping in the Robotics Database
structured_payload.candidate_goal: Use SSMS to inspect the Robotics database sort locations model and verify the association between sorted locations, queue locations, sorter sides, and sorter-entry sequence.

rough_steps: In SSMS, open the Robotics database and locate the sort locations database model/table.

Check the sorter-side association for each location and compare the recorded sequence with the sorter entrance queue order.

Check whether the Map Monitor displays the message "Currently in system emergency stop state." [Image support needed: RMS Map Monitor message area showing the system emergency-stop status.]

structured_payload.title: Remove/Recover a specific AGV by robot ID using OptiSweep→Geek API requests
structured_payload.summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API client to send a Geek request to remove a specified AGV from the system (RemoveAgv) or re-add it (RecoverAGV). Both API actions require the target robot ID.
structured_payload.when_to_use: When you need to remove a specific AGV from the system roster (RemoveAgv) or re-add it (RecoverAGV) by sending the correct OptiSweep→Geek API request using the required robot ID.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for identifying the correct robot ID; if the robot ID is incorrect/missing, the request cannot target the intended AGV.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Execute the OptiSweep / WCS API client requests (RemoveAgv / RecoverAGV) using the correct robot ID and verify the API client response indicates acceptance/success.

healthy_conditions: Error alert flag is true and bubbles to the top when an error exists (system error or “geek error”).

structured_payload.title: Check Windows Service State and Logs When the OptiSweep Gateway Is Unavailable
structured_payload.summary: Use Windows Event Viewer / services to inspect the relevant OptiSweep-related service, determine whether it is running or stopped, review available service or Event Viewer logs for crash or inactive-period evidence, and correlate the service state with gateway availability.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use this Windows Event Viewer / services diagnostic when the OptiSweep gateway is unavailable, does not open, or does not appear to be running, and a stopped service or service crash is suspected.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to restart a service or change service configuration; the supplied evidence supports inspection only.
Do not use this procedure as a complete recovery procedure when the service state or logs do not explain the gateway outage.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support performs the read-only Windows Event Viewer / services inspection and correlates service evidence with gateway availability.
Escalate when the service is stopped or inactive, the gateway remains unavailable, or available logs do not explain the outage.
safety_notes: This is a read-only diagnostic procedure.
Do not perform an unsupported service restart or configuration change based only on this procedure.

content.text: Use the live Ignition gateway's Lane Activity Model in the Sorter Sweeper Database view to determine whether incomplete package dimensions are associated with Scan Data 2, Induct, or SortConf records and whether the condition is concentrated on an auto-induct source. structured_payload.title: Diagnose Missing Package Dimensions in the Ignition Lane Activity Model
structured_payload.summary: Use the live Ignition gateway's Lane Activity Model in the Sorter Sweeper Database view to determine whether incomplete package dimensions are associated with Scan Data 2, Induct, or SortConf records and whether the condition is concentrated on an auto-induct source. Inspect package identifiers, tracking numbers, dimensional fields, cube, package classification, and MissingDimensionData.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use this live Ignition gateway diagnostic when sorter totes are overfilling or package data appears incomplete and support needs to determine whether default dimensions were used, which dimensional attribute is missing, and whether the condition is associated with a particular auto-induct source.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to change default dimensions, package classification, or database values.
Do not use this procedure to direct or perform dimensioner reboot or other physical equipment remediation.
Do not treat the observed MissingDimensionData rate as a universal pass/fail threshold; the source provides examples but no universal threshold.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support performs the live Ignition gateway inspection and interprets the Lane Activity Model records.
The site support contact or site operator provides the affected package, tracking number, operational symptoms, and any required physical equipment confirmation.
No role changes database values or package-dimension defaults as part of this diagnostic.
safety_notes: This is an inspection-only diagnostic. Do not modify default dimensions, package classification, or database values.
If physical dimensioner remediation is being considered, communicate the observed data condition to the site support contact rather than directing the physical action from this procedure.
access_or_tools_needed: Package ID or tracking number for the affected parcels

access_required: L2_support access to the Ignition gateway and the Sorter Sweeper Database view
system_preconditions: Recent lane activity records are available for inspection.
The affected package ID, package UID, or tracking number is available when record-level correlation is required.

visual_references.description: Ignition Lane Activity Model view showing message, package identifier, tracking number, dimensional fields, cube, package classification, and MissingDimensionData-related columns.
Lane activity records filtered to sort-confirmation data, illustrating repeated missing width, height, and weight values and correlation with an auto-induct source.
Lane Activity Model records used to inspect missing dimension data during a reported dimensioner-data interruption.

steps.title: Open the Ignition gateway Lane Activity Model
steps.purpose: Open the live sorter data view that records package messages and dimensional information.
steps.instruction: In the Ignition gateway, open the Sorter Sweeper Database view and select the Ignition Lane Activity Model.
steps.expected_result: The live Lane Activity Model displays recent sorter records with package, message, dimensional, cube, and missing-data fields.
steps.healthy_condition: The view loads and exposes recent records with identifiable package or tracking fields and a Message value.
steps.failure_condition: The Lane Activity Model does not load, contains no usable recent records, or does not expose the fields needed for package and dimension inspection.

actions.label: Open Lane Activity Model
actions.exact_action: Open the Sorter Sweeper Database view and select the Ignition Lane Activity Model.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the Ignition gateway view cannot be loaded or the required Lane Activity Model fields are unavailable.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The Ignition Lane Activity Model tracks Scan Data 2, Induct, and SortConf messages and displays package identifiers, tracking number, dimensions, weight, cube, package classification, and MissingDimensionData.

steps.title: Review recent Message records in the Ignition gateway
steps.purpose: Determine which sorter message types are represented in the affected recent records.
steps.instruction: In the Ignition gateway Lane Activity Model, review recent rows and inspect the Message field. Distinguish Scan Data 2, Induct, and SortConf records.
steps.expected_result: Recent rows can be categorized by Message value, showing whether the affected package data appears on Scan Data 2, Induct, or SortConf records.
steps.healthy_condition: The affected records have a readable Message value and can be related to a package or tracking identifier.
steps.failure_condition: The Message field is absent, unreadable, or cannot be associated with the affected records.

actions.label: Inspect message type
actions.exact_action: Review recent rows and use the Message field to distinguish Scan Data 2, Induct, and SortConf records.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if affected records cannot be associated with a package ID, tracking number, or message type.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The model listens to Scan Data 2, sort, and sort-confirm messages; the lane activity view shows which message is represented, including Induct and Scan Data 2.

steps.title: Inspect package and dimensional fields in the Ignition gateway
steps.purpose: Identify the package record and determine which dimensional values are present or missing.
steps.instruction: For the affected records in the Ignition gateway Lane Activity Model, inspect PackageLid or package ID, PackageUID where displayed, TrackingNumber, Length, Width, Height, Weight, Cube, PackageClassification, and MissingDimensionData.
steps.expected_result: The records show observable package identifiers and dimensional values, including any NULL or missing Length, Width, Height, or Weight values and the associated Cube value.
steps.healthy_condition: The affected record has sufficient package identification and dimensional values to compare the recorded dimensions with MissingDimensionData.
steps.failure_condition: The record cannot be identified, or required dimensional fields are unavailable for comparison.

actions.label: Inspect package attributes
actions.exact_action: Check PackageLid or package ID, TrackingNumber, Length, Width, Height, Weight, Cube, PackageClassification, and MissingDimensionData.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate when the table cannot associate affected records with a package ID or tracking number.
Escalate when the displayed dimensional data does not explain the reported sorter behavior.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The Lane Activity Model displays package UID, tracking number, length, height, weight, cube, package classification, and MissingDimensionData; the model description also identifies width.
The displayed Lane Activity Model columns include PackageUid, Tracking Number, Length, Width, Height, Weight, Cube, Message, PackageClassification, and Missing DimensionData.

steps.title: Interpret MissingDimensionData against the live dimensions
steps.purpose: Determine whether default dimensions were applied and identify the missing dimensional attribute.
steps.instruction: Compare MissingDimensionData with Length, Width, Height, Weight, and Cube for each affected record in the Ignition gateway Lane Activity Model. Treat MissingDimensionData=true as an indication that default dimensional values were used, then identify which dimensional field is NULL or otherwise missing.
steps.expected_result: The comparison identifies whether defaults were used and shows the missing attribute, such as Weight, Width, or Height, while retaining the observed Cube value.
steps.healthy_condition: MissingDimensionData is not true for the reviewed records, or any true value is explainable by the specific missing attribute shown in the dimensional fields.
steps.failure_condition: MissingDimensionData=true is present across affected records and the associated dimensional fields show missing values that can account for incomplete package data or overfilling.

actions.label: Compare missing-data flag
actions.exact_action: Compare the MissingDimensionData value with the dimensional fields and identify NULL or missing dimensional values.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if MissingDimensionData is true across a substantial set of recent records, especially when the records coincide with tote overfilling.
Do not assign a universal percentage threshold; the source does not define one.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: MissingDimensionData becomes true when default dimensions are used. Width and height commonly arrive together, while length is usually present but not always; an example identifies a high rate of missing weight data.

steps.title: Correlate missing dimensions with the auto-induct source
steps.purpose: Determine whether the missing-dimension condition is concentrated on one auto-induct source.
steps.instruction: Use the package ID or related induct identifier in the Ignition gateway Lane Activity Model to compare affected records from the same source, such as Auto Induct 1 or Auto Induct 2. Review the associated Message and dimensional fields for the grouped records.
steps.expected_result: The records show whether MissingDimensionData and the missing dimensional attribute are concentrated on one auto-induct source.
steps.healthy_condition: The affected records can be associated with an auto-induct source and do not show a source-specific pattern of missing dimensions.
steps.failure_condition: Records from one auto-induct source consistently show MissingDimensionData=true or repeated missing dimensional fields, such as missing width, height, or weight.

actions.label: Compare auto-induct sources
actions.exact_action: Use the package ID or related induct identifier to compare records from the same auto-induct source, such as Auto Induct 1 or Auto Induct 2.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if affected records cluster on one auto-induct source.
Escalate if the table cannot associate affected records with an induct source.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The lane activity records can be associated with Auto Induct 1 or Auto Induct 2 using the package ID; an example identifies Auto Induct 1 as the source of missing dimension data.
Filtering sort-confirmation records showed repeated width, height, and weight values and identified Auto Induct 1 as not sending sort or dimension data.

steps.title: Summarize the observed missing-dimension pattern
steps.purpose: Produce an evidence-based diagnostic summary for support escalation or site follow-up.
steps.instruction: Count or estimate the observed proportion of recent records with MissingDimensionData=true, identify the dominant missing field, record the relevant Message values and auto-induct source, and relate the findings to the reported sorter behavior. Do not apply a threshold that is not defined by the source.
steps.expected_result: The diagnostic summary states the observed MissingDimensionData condition, missing dimensional attribute, affected message type, package or tracking examples, associated auto-induct source, and any relationship to tote overfilling.
steps.healthy_condition: The observed records provide a coherent explanation of the package-dimension condition and do not show a broad unexplained pattern.
steps.failure_condition: A substantial or source-specific group of records has MissingDimensionData=true, repeated missing dimensions, or an unexplained relationship to the reported sorter behavior.

actions.label: Summarize observed pattern
actions.exact_action: Check the observed count or percentage of records with MissingDimensionData and note whether affected records are primarily missing weight, width, or height rather than length.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2 support or the site support contact if MissingDimensionData is true across a substantial set of recent records, especially when records cluster on one auto-induct source or coincide with tote overfilling.
Escalate when the displayed dimensional data does not explain the reported sorter behavior.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: MissingDimensionData supports counting incomplete dimensional data; the source gives examples of approximately 2% and approximately 29% missing dimensions but does not define a universal threshold.
A repeated missing-dimension pattern on sort-confirmation records was used to identify a dimension-data issue associated with Auto Induct 1.

success_criteria: The live Ignition gateway Lane Activity Model loads and provides recent records for inspection.
Affected records are categorized by Message value, including Scan Data 2, Induct, or SortConf where present.
Package identifiers, tracking numbers, dimensional fields, Cube, PackageClassification, and MissingDimensionData are compared.
The diagnostic identifies whether default dimensions were used and which dimensional attribute is missing.
The diagnostic determines whether the condition is concentrated on Auto Induct 1, Auto Induct 2, or another identifiable source.
The findings are summarized without changing database values, package classification, or default dimensions.
healthy_conditions: The Ignition gateway Lane Activity Model loads and displays recent package records.
Message values and package identifiers are available for correlation.
MissingDimensionData is not broadly true across the reviewed records.
Dimensional fields and Cube values are present or explain any MissingDimensionData=true result.
No unexplained auto-induct-specific concentration is observed.
failure_conditions: The Lane Activity Model cannot be loaded or required fields are unavailable.
Affected records cannot be associated with a package ID, tracking number, message type, or auto-induct source.
MissingDimensionData=true occurs across a substantial set of recent records.
Repeated NULL or missing Width, Height, or Weight values are concentrated on one auto-induct source.
The displayed dimensional data does not explain reported tote overfilling or incomplete package data.
escalation_guidance: Escalate to L2 support or the site support contact when MissingDimensionData is true across a substantial set of recent records, particularly when records cluster on one auto-induct source or coincide with tote overfilling.
Escalate when the Ignition gateway view cannot load or the table cannot associate affected records with package, message, or induct information.
Provide package or tracking identifiers, Message values, dimensional fields, Cube, MissingDimensionData, the observed count or percentage, and the associated auto-induct source.
Do not direct physical dimensioner remediation or change default dimensions as part of this diagnostic.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: The Ignition Lane Activity Model tracks Scan Data 2, Induct, and SortConf messages and displays package identifiers, tracking number, dimensions, weight, cube, package classification, MissingDimensionData, MissingInduct, Tote Not Found, Diverted, Off The End, and Recirc fields.

image_refs.what_to_look_at: The Ignition Lane Activity Model tracks Scan Data 2, Induct, and SortConf messages and displays package identifiers, tracking number, dimensions, weight, cube, package classification, MissingDimensionData, MissingInduct, Tote Not Found, Diverted, Off The End, and Recirc fields.

content.text: Use read-only SSMS access to the WCS / Helix Robotics Database to inspect active and completed AGV dwell records. Identify the AGV, station, SortGuid, and elapsed-time evidence associated with a tracked location dwell.

structured_payload.title: Diagnose AGV Location Dwell in the Robotics Database
structured_payload.summary: Use read-only SSMS access to the WCS / Helix Robotics Database to inspect active and completed AGV dwell records. Identify the AGV, station, SortGuid, and elapsed-time evidence associated with a tracked location dwell.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when investigating AGV waiting, idle time, or possible bottlenecks at a tracked hospital, tipper, or other station. Inspect the WCS / Helix Robotics Database in SSMS to determine whether the dwell is currently active or has been archived.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to modify DwellTracking settings or database records.
Do not use dwell records to identify a specific worker or tipper operator; the available evidence does not provide personnel cycling information.
Do not use this procedure as a complete throughput investigation or to optimize one location without considering system-level throughput.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Perform the read-only SSMS inspection of the WCS / Helix Robotics Database and interpret the active or completed dwell fields.
Review or assist when expected dwell evidence is missing or the displayed identifying or timing fields are insufficient for interpretation.

safety_notes: This is a read-only database diagnostic. Do not modify DwellTracking settings or database records.
Treat dwell information as system-throughput evidence. A dwell interval at one location may not represent the effect on overall system throughput.

access_required: L2 or L3 access to the WCS / Helix Robotics Database through SSMS
system_preconditions: The relevant station is configured for DwellTracking when an active dwell is expected.

visual_references.description: Robotics Database view showing LocationActiveDwellModel and LocationDwellActivity fields, including AgvName, Station, SortGuid, Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time.

steps.title: Open the Robotics Database in SSMS
steps.purpose: Access the WCS / Helix Robotics Database tables used to identify active and completed location dwell.
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), select the Robotics Database and locate the LocationActiveDwellModel and LocationDwellActivity tables.
steps.expected_result: The Robotics Database is selected and the two named dwell tables are available for read-only inspection.
steps.healthy_condition: SSMS provides access to the Robotics Database and the dwell tables can be inspected without changing data.
steps.failure_condition: The Robotics Database or either named dwell table is unavailable, or the access level would require modification of database records.

actions.label: Select Robotics Database
actions.exact_action: Open SSMS and select the Robotics Database.

actions.label: Locate dwell tables
actions.exact_action: Locate LocationActiveDwellModel and LocationDwellActivity.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3_support if the Robotics Database or named dwell tables cannot be accessed.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The Robotics Database contains LocationActiveDwellModel for active dwells and archives completed activity to LocationDwellActivity.

steps.title: Inspect active dwell records
steps.purpose: Determine whether an AGV is currently dwelling at a station configured for DwellTracking.
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect LocationActiveDwellModel for active rows at locations marked for DwellTracking. Review the AgvName, Station, and SortGuid fields.
steps.expected_result: An active dwell row, when present, identifies the AGV in AgvName, the tracked location in Station, and the associated sort in SortGuid.
steps.healthy_condition: The active row contains the displayed identifying fields: AgvName, Station, and SortGuid.
steps.failure_condition: A station expected to use DwellTracking has no active row, or the active row lacks AgvName, Station, or SortGuid needed for interpretation.

actions.label: Inspect active dwell model
actions.exact_action: Inspect LocationActiveDwellModel for locations marked for DwellTracking.

actions.label: Review active identifiers
actions.exact_action: Check AgvName, Station, and SortGuid for the active dwell record.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 engineering if a station expected to use DwellTracking has no corresponding active dwell evidence.
Escalate if the active record lacks the displayed identifying fields needed for interpretation.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: LocationActiveDwellModel displays active dwells at locations marked for DwellTracking with AgvName, Station, and SortGuid.

steps.title: Correlate the active row with the reported AGV station
steps.purpose: Check whether the active database association agrees with available live AGV location evidence.
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), compare the LocationActiveDwellModel Station and AgvName values with the AGV's current location or reported station when that evidence is available through the live support investigation.
steps.expected_result: The active database row associates the AGV named in AgvName with the station named in Station for the current dwell.
steps.healthy_condition: The available AGV location evidence is consistent with the active row's AgvName and Station.
steps.failure_condition: The available AGV location evidence conflicts with the active row, or no current-location evidence is available to perform the comparison.

actions.label: Compare AGV and station
actions.exact_action: Compare the active row's AgvName and Station with the AGV's current location or reported station when available.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate for further review if available live AGV location evidence conflicts with the active database row.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: An active dwell is collected when the AGV gets to a station configured for dwell tracking.

steps.title: Inspect the archived dwell activity
steps.purpose: Recover the completed dwell interval after the AGV has left the tracked location.
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect LocationDwellActivity for the AGV and station of interest. Review AgvName, Station, SortGuid, Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time.
steps.expected_result: A completed activity row contains the AGV, station, and sort identifiers together with Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time. A displayed interval may appear in a format such as 00:00:04.9803282.
steps.healthy_condition: The completed row contains the identifying and timing fields needed to establish the archived dwell interval.
steps.failure_condition: No completed activity is present after the AGV leaves the tracked location, or the row lacks AgvName, Station, SortGuid, Start Time, Finish Time, or Total Time.

actions.label: Open dwell activity archive
actions.exact_action: Inspect LocationDwellActivity after the AGV leaves the tracked location.

actions.label: Review completed fields
actions.exact_action: Check AgvName, Station, SortGuid, Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 engineering if expected completed dwell evidence is missing.
Escalate if the archived record lacks the displayed identifying or timing fields needed for interpretation.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Once the AGV leaves, the activity is archived to LocationDwellActivity with AgvName, Station, SortGuid, Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time.

steps.title: Interpret the dwell interval and station
steps.purpose: Use the archived timing and station values to characterize the observed dwell as operational evidence.
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), use the LocationDwellActivity Station and Total Time values to record the observed dwell interval and determine whether the live record names a hospital, tipper, or another tracked location.
steps.expected_result: The recorded result identifies the station named in Station and the elapsed interval shown in Total Time, such as 00:00:04.9803282.
steps.healthy_condition: The station and Total Time are visible and can be associated with the AGV and SortGuid in the same completed record.
steps.failure_condition: The station or Total Time is absent, or the record cannot be associated with an AGV and SortGuid.

actions.label: Record station and duration
actions.exact_action: Use the displayed Total Time and station values to record the observed dwell interval.

actions.label: Classify the tracked location
actions.exact_action: Identify whether the live Station value names a hospital, tipper, or other tracked location.

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not attribute a tipper dwell interval to a specific worker because personnel cycling information is not available in this evidence.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Dwell information is used to understand waiting, idle time, and possible bottlenecks, including hospital dwell and tipper dwell.

success_criteria: The WCS / Helix Robotics Database was inspected read-only through SSMS.
The active or completed dwell record was identified in LocationActiveDwellModel or LocationDwellActivity.
The result includes the available AgvName, Station, SortGuid, and timing fields.
For a completed dwell, the observed interval is taken from Total Time and associated with the station named in the live record.

structured_payload.title: Shut Down OptiSweep System Through the WCS API

structured_payload.when_to_use: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API when an authorized L2 or L3 support user needs to shut down the OptiSweep system from its live running state and verify the resulting system state.
not_for: Do not use POST System Shutdown unless GET System State confirms that the system is running.
Do not use this procedure as a physical emergency stop or a substitute for site safety actions.

steps.instruction: For the same tote/parcel context, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for scan-derived parcel dimensions and load category fields that are described as coming from the scan tunnel onto the chat.
steps.expected_result: Dimensions and load category fields are populated for the parcel/tote context.
steps.healthy_condition: Dimension and load category values are present (not null/empty) for the same tote/parcel identifier that has induction evidence.
steps.failure_condition: Scan-derived dimensions and/or load category are missing or not populated for the tote/parcel in process.

actions.label: Query scan data evidence
actions.exact_action: Query for scan/parcel data collection evidence (dimensions and load category) that is described as coming from the scan tunnel onto the chat.

stop_or_escalate_if: If scan-derived dimensions/load category are missing while induction evidence exists, escalate for deeper module-level investigation (Sorter Sweeper vs XLE COM vs OPC COM).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “We listen to scan data too, which is from the scan tunnel. We collect the dimensions of the parcel and the load category.”
Example evidence view includes columns for TrackingNumber and Length/Width/Height/Weight (dimension fields) alongside sort confirmation filtering.

steps.title: Verify sort confirmation evidence includes final destination
steps.purpose: Confirm the sort stage is completed and that the parcel has a final destination in the confirmation evidence.
steps.instruction: For the same tote/parcel, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for sort confirmation records. Confirm that a sort confirmation record exists and includes a final destination for the parcel.
steps.expected_result: A sort confirmation evidence record exists for the tote/parcel and includes a final destination.
steps.healthy_condition: Sort confirmation evidence is present and shows a final destination value for the same tote/parcel identifier.
steps.failure_condition: Sort confirmation evidence is missing, or it exists without a final destination value.

actions.label: Query sort confirmation
actions.exact_action: Query for sort confirmation evidence that sort was sent from XLE onto the chat and that a sort confirmation was sent from the sorter onto the chat.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if sort confirmation evidence is missing for the tote/parcel.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “Sort is sent from XLE so it's UPS version of WCS on to the chat… We collect the possible destinations for each parcel and then we get a sort confirmation as sent from the sorter onto the chat.”

steps.title: Verify hot bin closeout / hop-in exchange evidence (when expected)
steps.purpose: Confirm the hot bin/hop-in closeout path triggers an exchange immediately when UPS sends the hot bin message.
steps.instruction: If the tote(s) are expected to be hop-in/hot-bin, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for hot bin message/hop-in message records for those totes. Confirm that the exchange-related state advances immediately after the hot bin/hop-in evidence.
steps.expected_result: Hot bin/hop-in evidence exists for the tote(s) and exchange-related state advances immediately after.
steps.healthy_condition: For hop-in/hot-bin totes, hot bin/hop-in evidence is present and exchange advancement is observable in the evidence timeline for the same tote(s).
steps.failure_condition: Hot bin/hop-in evidence is missing when expected, or exchange advancement does not occur immediately after hot bin/hop-in evidence.

actions.label: Query hot bin/hop-in evidence
actions.exact_action: Query for a hot bin message/hop-in message for totes that are hop in and confirm an exchange is triggered immediately.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if hot bin/hop-in evidence is missing for totes that are expected to be hop-in.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “UPS can trigger a hop in close out by sending us a hop in message for all totes that are hop in and we do an exchange immediately.”

steps.title: Verify destination close message exists before exchange advancement
steps.purpose: Confirm the destination close stage is sent before the exchange occurs.
steps.instruction: Before the exchange-related state advances for the tote/parcel, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for a destination close message being sent onto the chat. Correlate it to the destination tied to the tote.
steps.expected_result: A destination close message evidence record exists for the destination tied to the tote before exchange-related state advances.
steps.healthy_condition: Destination close evidence is present and occurs earlier in the evidence timeline than exchange advancement for the same tote/parcel.
steps.failure_condition: Destination close message is missing, or exchange advancement occurs without destination close evidence preceding it.

actions.label: Query destination close evidence
actions.exact_action: Before an exchange, query for a destination close message being sent onto the chat.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if destination close message is missing before the exchange-related state advances.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “And then when the totes is ready to leave… we send the destination close message onto the chat before we do an exchange.”

steps.title: Verify print label message is sent at the tipper stage
steps.purpose: Confirm the final stage: label print trigger message is sent to the printer with the label provided by XLE.
steps.instruction: At the tipper stage for the tote/parcel, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for a print label message being sent to the printer. Confirm it is associated with the label provided by XLE (e.g., label payload/identifier present).
steps.expected_result: A print label message evidence record exists and is associated with the label provided by XLE (label payload/identifier present).
steps.healthy_condition: Print label evidence is present for the tote/parcel at the tipper stage and includes an associated label identifier/payload.
steps.failure_condition: Print label message evidence is missing at the tipper stage.

actions.label: Query print label evidence
actions.exact_action: At the tipper stage, query for a print label message being sent to the printer.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if print label message evidence is missing at the tipper stage.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “And then at the tipper, we send a print label message to the printer so it can print a label provided by the XLE.”

steps.title: Stop and escalate on missing/out-of-order message evidence
steps.purpose: Ensure rapid escalation when the required message sequence is incomplete or out of order for the same tote/parcel.
steps.instruction: If any required message evidence is missing or out of order for the same tote/parcel (tote inducted present but destination enabled missing; sort confirmation missing; destination close missing before exchange; print label missing at tipper), stop further checks and escalate for deeper module-level investigation.
steps.expected_result: A clear escalation decision is made based on which message evidence is missing/out of order.
steps.healthy_condition: All required message evidence is present in the expected order for the tote/parcel under investigation.
steps.failure_condition: Any required evidence is missing or the order is violated for the same tote/parcel.

actions.label: Escalate based on evidence gap
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if any required message evidence is missing (e.g., tote inducted present but destination enabled missing; sort confirmation missing; destination close missing before exchange; print label message missing at tipper).

stop_or_escalate_if: tote inducted present but destination enabled missing
sort confirmation missing
destination close missing before exchange
print label message missing at tipper
only one side present (e.g., scan data present but sort confirmation missing)

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The segment defines the required ordered sequence and the hot bin closeout/destination close/print label triggers that must occur for the tote lifecycle.

If hop-in/hot-bin is expected, hot bin/hop-in evidence exists and exchange advancement occurs immediately.

structured_payload.summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) to inspect the read-only dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel view and determine whether recent lane activity records contain dimension data expected from the dimensioners. structured_payload.title: Start OptiSweep System Through the WCS API
structured_payload.summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API through Apidog or an equivalent approved API client to start the system from a shutdown state, then verify the live system state is no longer shutdown.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API when the live system state is shutdown and an authorized L2 or L3 support user needs to start the system through the System Startup operation.
not_for: Do not use when GET System State does not report shutdown.
Do not use as a substitute for investigating an API request that cannot be executed or returns an unrecognized result.
Do not use this procedure to perform physical recovery, E-stop, or LOTO actions.

steps.title: If AGV already left, verify archived dwell activity in “Location Dwell activity”

steps.failure_condition: Dwell records appear inconsistent between active and archived tables (e.g., missing from both, or present in active when it should have been archived).

actions.label: Check archived dwell activity

stop_or_escalate_if: If dwell records appear inconsistent between active and archived tables, escalate for support to reconcile the timing/archival behavior.

structured_payload.title: Check AGV State, Command Vitals, and Errors in the OptiSweep WCS API
structured_payload.summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API through Apidog to inspect an AGV's live state, current command fields, vitals, network identity, AGV errors, system errors, and errorAlert indicator.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use this Apidog / OptiSweep WCS API diagnostic when support needs to verify an AGV's live state, current command information, vitals, network identity, or AGV and system error indications.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to remove, recover, pause, resume, or execute an AGV command.
Do not use this procedure to infer a healthy battery or voltage range; the source provides example values but no complete operating thresholds.
Do not use this procedure as a physical AGV recovery or E-stop procedure.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support may perform the read-only inspection through the Apidog / OptiSweep WCS API client.
Escalate to L2_support when the response cannot be obtained, required fields are unavailable, or reported AGV or system errors require further investigation.
safety_notes: This procedure is diagnostic and does not direct a production stop, physical intervention, or AGV control request.
Do not substitute a control request such as PauseAgvs, RemoveAgv, RecoverAgv, or Resend Geek Command for this read-only status inspection.

steps.title: Inspect AGV and system errors in the Apidog WCS API response

structured_payload.summary: Use the Ignition Gateway UI to check the current OPC Connections status for specific tipper endpoints. Confirm whether the expected tipper entries show “Faulted” (example: tipper 7 and 8 powered off show “Faulted”).

structured_payload.title: Check Ignition Gateway Performance Metrics
structured_payload.summary: An L2 support user can open the live Ignition gateway performance page in a web browser and review CPU, memory, connection, response-time, slow-response, garbage-collector, and tuning-script indicators for evidence of gateway health or degradation.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use this Ignition gateway diagnostic procedure when gateway health, performance degradation, an unplanned restart, or related OPC and application symptoms require live evidence from the Ignition Gateway performance page.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for a physical E-stop, LOTO, or physical AGV recovery.
Do not infer numeric healthy thresholds for CPU, memory, response time, garbage collectors, or other indicators from this procedure.
Do not restart services or change gateway configuration as part of this inspection-only procedure.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Open the Ignition gateway performance page and inspect the displayed live indicators.
Support interpretation or escalation when gateway performance evidence indicates degradation or the page cannot be opened.

safety_notes: This is a diagnostic inspection procedure; do not change gateway settings or restart services based only on this runbook.
Preserve displayed response events, severity values, and visible trend behavior as escalation evidence.

steps.healthy_condition: No unexplained visible CPU or memory spike or sustained elevated activity is present in the displayed trends.
steps.failure_condition: A visible CPU or memory spike, sustained elevated activity, or a memory spike followed by a drop to zero is present without an explained event.

steps.title: Verify lifecycle progression: sent time and in-progress time
steps.purpose: Determine whether the command is still active and whether it has progressed from sent to in-progress.
steps.instruction: Observe the lifecycle timestamps/fields for the targeted row: confirm whether the row shows a sent time and whether it has transitioned to an in-progress state (in-progress time populated).
steps.expected_result: For the targeted command row, sent time is populated; in-progress time is populated if the command has progressed to in-progress.
steps.healthy_condition: Sent time is populated; in-progress time is populated when the AGV is marked as in-progress for that command.

actions.label: Check sent vs in-progress timestamps
actions.exact_action: Observe the lifecycle timestamps/fields: confirm whether the row shows a sent time and whether it has transitioned to an in-progress state (in-progress time populated).

stop_or_escalate_if: If the command remains in RobotCommandDatabaseModel without an in-progress transition (sent time populated but in-progress time not populated), escalate for deeper command/task state troubleshooting rather than assuming completion.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: When we write it to the table, we put sent; when we get in progress is when we mark that AGV. This shows you the sent time and in progress time.

steps.title: Check destination/queue-capacity interaction evidence for in-progress commands
steps.purpose: Corroborate that in-progress status corresponds to active queue/location occupancy behavior.
steps.instruction: If the command is in-progress, confirm queue/capacity interaction evidence by checking that the destination queue/location is reflected as freed/occupied based on in-progress status (e.g., in-progress indicates the AGV is occupying the queue/location capacity).
steps.expected_result: The destination/current location fields associated with the in-progress command reflect active occupancy behavior consistent with queue capacity handling.
steps.healthy_condition: In-progress status aligns with queue/location occupancy freeing/occupying behavior described by the robot location model (max AGVs per queue/location).
steps.failure_condition: In-progress status does not align with expected occupancy/capacity evidence for the destination queue/location.

actions.label: Corroborate queue/location occupancy evidence
actions.exact_action: Confirm queue/capacity interaction evidence by checking that the destination queue/location is reflected as freed/occupied based on in-progress status.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Until we get it in progress, you still have current destination location; in the robot location model you have Max Agvs, and each tipper can only have one (some have two). When it is in progress, we freed up that queue, that location.

steps.failure_condition: The command appears completed but is still present in RobotCommandDatabaseModel, or the command cannot be found in either active or archived records.

steps.expected_result: Recent SortConf rows are visible in dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel with lane, package, dimension, classification, and sorter-event fields.
steps.healthy_condition: Recent SortConf rows are present and include observable values such as TrackingNumber, package or tote identifiers, lane information, and the available dimension and event fields.
steps.failure_condition: No recent SortConf rows are present, or the returned records do not expose the expected lane activity fields.

actions.label: Filter lane activity
actions.exact_action: Filter dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel where Message = "SortConf" and review the recent results.

stop_or_escalate_if: Recent SortConf records are absent from dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: OCR shows a query against dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel with Message = "SortConf" and results ordered by Id desc.
The SSMS results are filtered on sort confirmation to inspect whether AI1 is sending sort and dimension data.

steps.title: Inspect dimension and sorter-event fields
steps.purpose: Determine whether the SortConf records contain package dimensions and indicators associated with missing or abnormal sorter data.
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) SortConf results, inspect TrackingNumber, Length, Width, Height, Weight, and Cube. Also inspect MissingDimensionData, MissingInduct, ToteNotFound, Diverted, OffTheEnd, and Recirc for the same records.
steps.expected_result: The selected SortConf rows show which package dimension fields are populated and the corresponding values of the sorter-event indicators.
steps.healthy_condition: Recent records contain dimension values when dimension data is available, and the event-indicator fields do not show a consistently abnormal pattern across the records being reviewed.
steps.failure_condition: Dimension fields are consistently null, blank, or defaulted; MissingDimensionData is repeatedly asserted; or ToteNotFound, Diverted, OffTheEnd, Recirc, or related indicators show an unexplained abnormal pattern.

actions.label: Inspect dimension fields
actions.exact_action: Review TrackingNumber, Length, Width, Height, Weight, and Cube in the SortConf results.

actions.label: Inspect event indicators
actions.exact_action: Review MissingDimensionData, MissingInduct, ToteNotFound, Diverted, OffTheEnd, and Recirc in the SortConf results.

stop_or_escalate_if: Dimension fields are consistently missing or defaulted.
The event indicators show an abnormal pattern that cannot be explained from the available WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) records.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: OCR lists TrackingNumber, Length, Height, Weight, Cube, Message, PackageClassification, MissingDimensionData, MissingInduct, ToteNotFound, Diverted, OffTheEnd, and Recirc.
The observed example states that Width, Height, and Weight were consistently 1 in the filtered SortConf results, indicating that AI1 was not sending sort or dimension data.

steps.title: Compare the records with the reported condition
steps.purpose: Relate the live WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) observations to the reported AI1, default-dimension, or tote-overflow condition.
steps.instruction: Compare the recent SortConf dimension values and event indicators in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) with the reported condition. Treat repeated missing or defaulted dimensions together with MissingDimensionData or the reported AI1 data loss as evidence that the lane activity is not receiving expected dimension data. Do not infer a cause beyond the records.
steps.expected_result: The diagnostic identifies whether the live SortConf records support or do not support the reported missing-dimension or tote-overflow condition.
steps.healthy_condition: Recent SortConf records contain usable dimension values for the reviewed records and do not consistently indicate missing dimension data.
steps.failure_condition: The records show absent AI1-related activity, repeated defaulted or missing dimensions, or a pattern consistent with the reported tote overflow that cannot be explained by the available records.

actions.label: Correlate live records
actions.exact_action: Compare the recent SortConf records with the reported AI1 data loss, default dimensions, or tote overflow.

stop_or_escalate_if: AI1-related data is not represented in recent lane activity records.
Default dimensions or tote overflow continue and the available records do not explain the condition.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The support example links tote overflow with AI1 not sending data and the use of default dimensions.
The example associates a power flicker with dimension data not rebooting properly and directs support to identify missing dimension data in the database.

steps.title: Stop the read-only diagnostic and escalate unexplained findings
steps.purpose: Prevent unsupported database or equipment changes and route conditions that cannot be explained from the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) evidence.
steps.instruction: Stop the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) inspection without modifying records or configuration when recent SortConf rows are absent, dimensions remain consistently missing or defaulted, or event indicators show an unexplained abnormal pattern. Escalate the evidence and the reported operating condition to L3_support.
steps.expected_result: The diagnostic ends with the observed database evidence preserved for escalation and no database or configuration changes made.
steps.healthy_condition: The investigation can be concluded from recent SortConf records without unexplained missing data or abnormal indicator patterns.
steps.failure_condition: The available WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) records cannot account for the reported AI1, default-dimension, or tote-overflow condition.

actions.label: Escalate evidence
actions.exact_action: Stop the read-only diagnostic and escalate when the recent SortConf records or indicators do not explain the condition.

stop_or_escalate_if: Recent SortConf records are absent.
Dimension fields are consistently missing or defaulted.
Event indicators show an abnormal pattern that cannot be explained from the available records.
Tote overflow continues while AI1 data or expected dimension data is not represented in the lane activity records.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The candidate source supports checking the lane activity model and escalating when AI1 data is absent or default dimensions and tote overflow continue.

success_criteria: Recent SortConf rows are located in dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel using the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).
TrackingNumber, Length, Width, Height, Weight, Cube, and the listed sorter-event indicators are inspected.
The records provide live evidence for or against missing dimension data, AI1 data loss, default dimensions, or tote overflow.
No database records or configuration are modified.
healthy_conditions: Recent SortConf records are present in dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel.
Dimension values are populated when dimension data is available.
MissingDimensionData and related event indicators do not show a consistently unexplained abnormal pattern.
failure_conditions: Recent SortConf records are absent.
TrackingNumber or dimension fields are consistently missing, blank, null, or defaulted.

AI1-related data is not represented in recent lane activity records.
Tote overflow continues and the available SortConf records do not explain the condition.
escalation_guidance: Escalate to L3_support when recent SortConf records are absent or the available WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) evidence cannot explain the reported condition.
Include the reviewed database, table, SortConf filter, affected dimension fields, and observed event-indicator pattern in the escalation.
