content.text: Use the S-Tunnel / Chat path display on the remotely accessed WCS primary computer to inspect the connection list, active connection count, service names, traffic counters, and TLS status.

structured_payload.title: Check S-Tunnel Active Connections and TLS Status
structured_payload.summary: Use the S-Tunnel / Chat path display on the remotely accessed WCS primary computer to inspect the connection list, active connection count, service names, traffic counters, and TLS status.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when verifying whether the live S-Tunnel / Chat path on the WCS primary computer has the expected service connections and successful TLS session status.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a recovery or restart procedure; the source provides connection and TLS inspection only.
Do not treat an isolated "No peer certificate received" message as a recovery instruction. Escalate for interpretation when it conflicts with the overall S-Tunnel / Chat path status.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Remotely access the WCS primary computer and inspect the live S-Tunnel / Chat path connection view and log.
Interpret or escalate inconsistent connection counts, missing services, or TLS status when L2 support cannot determine the condition.

safety_notes: This is an inspection-only diagnostic. Do not restart S-Tunnel or other services based solely on this procedure.
Do not infer recovery from an isolated "No peer certificate received" message.
access_or_tools_needed: Remote access to the WCS primary computer

access_required: L2 or L3 support access to the WCS primary computer
Access to the S-Tunnel / Chat path display
system_preconditions: The S-Tunnel / Chat path application is available on the WCS primary computer.

visual_references.description: S-Tunnel / Chat path display showing the File menu, connections view, active connection messages, service names, traffic counters, and TLS log status.

steps.title: Open the S-Tunnel / Chat path on the WCS primary computer
steps.purpose: Open the live S-Tunnel / Chat path display so its connection log and connection controls can be inspected.
steps.instruction: Using remote access to the WCS primary computer, open the S-Tunnel / Chat path application.
steps.expected_result: The S-Tunnel / Chat path window is visible with its connection log and menu bar.
steps.healthy_condition: The S-Tunnel / Chat path application opens and its log area is available for inspection.
steps.failure_condition: The S-Tunnel / Chat path application cannot be opened or its connection log is unavailable.

actions.label: Open S-Tunnel
actions.exact_action: Open the S-Tunnel / Chat path application on the WCS primary computer.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support if the S-Tunnel / Chat path application cannot be opened or the connection log is unavailable.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The captured S-Tunnel screen is accessed on the computer and shows the S-Tunnel connection log and menu bar.

steps.title: Open the S-Tunnel connections view
steps.purpose: Navigate to the live connection list used to inspect active S-Tunnel / Chat path services.
steps.instruction: In the S-Tunnel / Chat path application, open the File menu and select the connections option.
steps.expected_result: The S-Tunnel connections view opens and displays the active connection information.
steps.healthy_condition: The connections view is visible and contains connection entries or active-connection status information.
steps.failure_condition: The File menu does not provide the connections option, or the connections view does not open.

actions.label: Open connections
actions.exact_action: Under the S-Tunnel application's File menu, click connections.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support if the connections option is unavailable or the connections view cannot be opened.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The S-Tunnel display instructs the user to click connections under File.

steps.title: Inspect the active service connection list
steps.purpose: Verify that the expected S-Tunnel / Chat path services are represented in the live connection list.
steps.instruction: In the S-Tunnel connections view, inspect the active connection list for the expected service connections, including AI01, AI02, and SortationChat where displayed.
steps.expected_result: The active connection list shows the expected service entries, including AI01, AI02, and SortationChat where displayed.
steps.healthy_condition: The expected service connections are present in the active connection list.
steps.failure_condition: An expected service connection is missing from the active connection list.

actions.label: Inspect service entries
actions.exact_action: Check the active connection list for AI01, AI02, and SortationChat where displayed.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if an expected service connection is missing.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The S-Tunnel display states that it should show 3 connections including AI01, AI02, and SortationChat.

steps.title: Verify active connection count and traffic counters
steps.purpose: Confirm the expected number of active S-Tunnel / Chat path connections and verify that the live services show traffic counters.
steps.instruction: In the S-Tunnel connections view and log, confirm that the display reports 3 active connection(s). Review the per-service bytes sent to TLS and bytes sent to socket counters.
steps.expected_result: The display reports 3 active connection(s), and the active service entries show bytes sent to TLS and bytes sent to socket counters.
steps.healthy_condition: The S-Tunnel / Chat path reports 3 active connection(s) and the service entries contain traffic-counter values.
steps.failure_condition: The active connection count is not 3, or the expected service entries do not show traffic-counter information.

actions.label: Check active count
actions.exact_action: Confirm that the display reports 3 active connection(s).

actions.label: Review traffic counters
actions.exact_action: Review the per-service bytes sent to TLS and bytes sent to socket counters.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the active connection count is not 3.
Escalate if the expected service entries do not show the traffic counters needed to assess the connection.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The S-Tunnel log reports Listed 3 active connection(s) and shows per-service bytes sent to TLS and bytes sent to socket.

steps.title: Verify successful TLS status in the connection log
steps.purpose: Confirm that the active S-Tunnel / Chat path connections have observable successful TLS session status.
steps.instruction: Review the S-Tunnel connection log for messages including "TLS negotiation finished successfully" and, where present, session reuse or a connected status.
steps.expected_result: The connection log contains successful TLS negotiation messages and may also show session reuse, a connected status, TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, or authenticated application data.
steps.healthy_condition: The live S-Tunnel log shows "TLS negotiation finished successfully" for the relevant connection and/or a connected status with session reuse.
steps.failure_condition: The connection log does not show successful TLS negotiation or connected-status evidence for an expected active connection.

actions.label: Check TLS messages
actions.exact_action: Check the connection log for "TLS negotiation finished successfully" and, where present, session reuse or a connected status.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the connection log does not show successful TLS negotiation.
Do not treat an isolated "No peer certificate received" message as a recovery instruction; escalate for interpretation if it conflicts with the overall connection status.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The S-Tunnel log contains successful TLS negotiation, session reuse, connected status, TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, authenticated application data, and a No peer certificate received message.

success_criteria: The S-Tunnel / Chat path connections view is open on the WCS primary computer.
The expected service connections, including AI01, AI02, and SortationChat where displayed, are present.
The display reports 3 active connection(s).
Per-service bytes sent to TLS and bytes sent to socket counters are visible.
The connection log shows "TLS negotiation finished successfully" and, where present, session reuse or connected status.
healthy_conditions: The S-Tunnel / Chat path reports 3 active connection(s).
Expected service names are present in the active connection list.
Active services show traffic counters for bytes sent to TLS and bytes sent to socket.
The connection log shows successful TLS negotiation and observable connected or session-reuse status.
failure_conditions: The active connection count is not 3.
An expected service connection is missing.
Traffic counters are absent for an expected active service.
The connection log lacks successful TLS negotiation or connected-status evidence.
An isolated "No peer certificate received" message conflicts with the overall connection status and requires interpretation.
escalation_guidance: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the active connection count is not 3, an expected service connection is missing, or successful TLS negotiation is not shown.
Do not restart S-Tunnel or other services under this diagnostic; the source does not provide a recovery or restart procedure.
Escalate an isolated "No peer certificate received" message for interpretation when it conflicts with the overall connection status.

screens_or_images.what_to_look_at: S-Tunnel / Chat path window showing the File menu and connections option, service names including AI01, AI02, and SortationChat where displayed, the 3 active connection(s) status, TLS and socket byte counters, and TLS log messages.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: The captured S-Tunnel screen instructs the user to click connections under File, shows expected connections including AI01 and AI02, and reports 3 active connection(s) with TLS status and traffic counters.

image_refs.what_to_look_at: S-Tunnel / Chat path window showing the File menu and connections option, service names including AI01, AI02, and SortationChat where displayed, the 3 active connection(s) status, TLS and socket byte counters, and TLS log messages.

missing_details: The source does not specify the remote-access method or connection path to the WCS primary computer.
The source does not provide a recovery, restart, certificate-remediation, or service-restoration procedure.
The source does not define an authoritative mapping for every displayed service name or specify required byte-counter thresholds.
The source does not establish whether the S-Tunnel window must be opened through Windows Services or another launcher.

content.text: Use read-only SSMS access to the WCS / Helix Sorter Sweeper Database to inspect Tipper Departure Activity Model records and Tag Read/Tag Write log values associated with an AGV departure. Review the departure destination, tote identifier, fault information, tag path, and recorded value to narrow down a tipper issue without inferring undocumented fault-code meanings or corrective actions.

structured_payload.title: Diagnose Tipper Issues in SSMS Using Sorter Sweeper Database Tipper Departure and Tag Logs
structured_payload.summary: Use read-only SSMS access to the WCS / Helix Sorter Sweeper Database to inspect Tipper Departure Activity Model records and Tag Read/Tag Write log values associated with an AGV departure. Review the departure destination, tote identifier, fault information, tag path, and recorded value to narrow down a tipper issue without inferring undocumented fault-code meanings or corrective actions.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use this SSMS / WCS / Helix DB diagnostic when investigating a tipper issue and a corresponding AGV departure from a tipper, DropOffSorter, or DropOffHospital needs to be checked in the Sorter Sweeper Database.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to change database records, perform recovery, or prescribe corrective action.
Do not infer the meaning of a fault code from the recorded database value alone.
Do not use this procedure as a replacement for physical intervention or an operational stop.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support performs the read-only inspection in SSMS against the WCS / Helix Sorter Sweeper Database.
L3_support may review or receive the escalation when records are missing, contain fault information, or cannot be correlated.
safety_notes: Use read-only SSMS inspection only.
Do not modify database records or infer an unverified fault-code meaning or corrective action.
access_or_tools_needed: Tag Read and Tag Write logs

access_required: L2_support access to the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) surface
system_preconditions: A relevant AGV departure from a tipper, DropOffSorter, or DropOffHospital has been identified for inspection.

visual_references.description: Sorter Sweeper Database view showing Tipper Departure Activity Model records and Tag Read/Tag Write log fields, including Task Name, ToteId, Fault, TagPath, and Value.

steps.title: Open the Sorter Sweeper Database records in SSMS
steps.purpose: Locate the live WCS database records needed to investigate the tipper departure.
steps.instruction: In SSMS on the WCS / Helix DB surface, open the Sorter Sweeper Database and locate the Tipper Departure Activity Model records and the Tag Read and Tag Write log view or model. Use the available record display without modifying data.
steps.expected_result: The live SSMS display exposes Tipper Departure Activity Model records and Tag Read/Tag Write entries with recorded tag paths and values.
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant database records and log fields are available for inspection.
steps.failure_condition: The Sorter Sweeper Database records or Tag Read/Tag Write fields cannot be located or accessed.

actions.label: Inspect Sorter Sweeper Database
actions.exact_action: Open the Sorter Sweeper Database and locate the Tipper Departure Activity Model records and Tag Read and Tag Write log view or model.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the expected Sorter Sweeper Database records or log fields are unavailable.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The Sorter Sweeper Database contains Tipper Departure Activity Model records, and Tag Read and Tag Write logs record tags the system reads and writes.

steps.title: Locate the relevant departure record
steps.purpose: Find the database record corresponding to the AGV departure being investigated.
steps.instruction: In the SSMS Tipper Departure Activity Model records, review the entries for the relevant AGV departure from a tipper, DropOffSorter, or DropOffHospital.
steps.expected_result: A departure record is identified for the relevant tipper, DropOffSorter, or DropOffHospital event.
steps.healthy_condition: A corresponding departure record is present and identifies the applicable departure destination type or task.
steps.failure_condition: No corresponding departure record can be found for the relevant event.

actions.label: Review departure records
actions.exact_action: Review the departure records for the relevant AGV departure from a tipper, DropOffSorter, or DropOffHospital.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the expected departure record is missing.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Every time an AGV is sent away from the tipper, DropOffSorter, or DropOffHospital, a Tipper Departure Activity Model record is recorded.

steps.title: Inspect the departure and tag log fields
steps.purpose: Capture the observable database values associated with the departure and its tag activity.
steps.instruction: In the live SSMS record display, inspect the Task Name, ToteId, Fault or fault-code field, TagPath, and Value fields for the relevant departure and associated Tag Read/Tag Write entries.
steps.expected_result: The record display provides the Task Name, ToteId, Fault or fault-code information, TagPath, and Value associated with the departure or tag log entry.
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant departure and tag entries expose the fields needed for comparison, including a recorded tag path and value where applicable.
steps.failure_condition: One or more expected fields are absent, unreadable, or contain associated fault information requiring further review.

actions.label: Inspect record fields
actions.exact_action: Check the displayed Task Name, ToteId, Fault or fault code, TagPath, and Value fields for the departure record.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the record has an associated fault code.
Escalate if the expected Task Name, ToteId, Fault, TagPath, or Value fields cannot be inspected.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: OCR shows fields including Task Name, ToteId, Fault, TagPath, and Value. The tote, tag path, and any fault code are recorded for the departure.

steps.title: Correlate tag values with the departure record
steps.purpose: Determine whether the tag activity is represented consistently with the associated departure and recorded fault information.
steps.instruction: In SSMS, compare the TagPath and Value from the Tag Read/Tag Write entries with the relevant Tipper Departure Activity Model record, including its Task Name, ToteId, departure destination, and Fault or fault-code information. Treat the displayed values as recorded data; do not assign an undocumented meaning to a fault code.
steps.expected_result: The tag path and value can be associated with the relevant departure record, or the record shows that the event cannot be correlated.
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant departure record and Tag Read/Tag Write entries are present and their Task Name, ToteId, TagPath, Value, and available fault information can be correlated.
steps.failure_condition: The TagPath and Value cannot be correlated with the departure event, the departure record is missing, or the record contains fault information requiring escalation.

actions.label: Compare departure and tag entries
actions.exact_action: Compare the recorded tag path and value with the associated departure and fault-code information to determine whether the event is represented in the logs.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the TagPath and Value cannot be correlated with the tipper event.
Do not infer a fault-code meaning or corrective action when the database record only provides the recorded value.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Recorded tote, tag path, and fault-code information, together with Tag Read and Tag Write values, can help narrow down tipper issues.

success_criteria: A corresponding Tipper Departure Activity Model record is identified for the relevant tipper, DropOffSorter, or DropOffHospital departure.
The live SSMS display provides the applicable Task Name, ToteId, Fault or fault-code information, TagPath, and Value fields.
Tag Read/Tag Write entries can be correlated with the associated departure record, or the inability to correlate them is clearly identified for escalation.
No database mutation or unsupported fault-code interpretation is performed.
healthy_conditions: The Sorter Sweeper Database is accessible through SSMS.
A relevant Tipper Departure Activity Model record is present.
The departure and tag entries expose observable Task Name, ToteId, TagPath, Value, and available Fault information.
The recorded TagPath and Value can be associated with the relevant departure event.
failure_conditions: The expected departure record is missing.
The record contains an associated fault code.
Task Name, ToteId, Fault, TagPath, or Value cannot be inspected.
TagPath and Value cannot be correlated with the tipper departure.
The available database value does not support a verified fault-code meaning or corrective action.
escalation_guidance: Escalate to L3_support or the applicable engineering support path when the expected departure record is missing, the record has an associated fault code, or TagPath and Value cannot be correlated with the tipper event.
Provide the observed Task Name, ToteId, Fault or fault-code value, TagPath, Value, and the associated departure destination in the escalation.
Do not infer a fault-code meaning or corrective action from the database record alone.

screens_or_images.what_to_look_at: Sorter Sweeper Database Tipper Departure Activity Model records and Tag Read/Tag Write fields, especially Task Name, ToteId, Fault, TagPath, and Value.

content.text: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only surface to inspect the Sorter Sweeper Database Tipper model for the relevant operator station. Verify the Tipper ID and station association, Printer Name and printer IP when configured, Location ID, and Tipper Status.

structured_payload.title: Check Tipper Model Station, Printer, and Tipper Status Fields
structured_payload.summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only surface to inspect the Sorter Sweeper Database Tipper model for the relevant operator station. Verify the Tipper ID and station association, Printer Name and printer IP when configured, Location ID, and Tipper Status.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when support needs to verify the live tipper configuration used by the system, including the station-to-tipper association, printer configuration, location association, or current Tipper Status in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).
not_for: Changing printer, location, station, or tipper-status configuration.
Operating or recovering a tipper through the Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU.
Replacing a live equipment fault investigation with configuration inspection alone.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Perform the read-only inspection in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and record the observed Tipper model values.
Review or assist with inconsistent, missing, Not Ready, or Disabled Tipper model records.

safety_notes: Use read-only inspection only. This procedure does not authorize changing printer, location, station, or status configuration.
A Not Ready or Disabled value is an observed configuration/status condition and requires escalation rather than an in-procedure change.

access_required: L2/L3 access to the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only surface.
system_preconditions: The relevant operator station or tipper must be identified before inspecting the Tipper model record.
external_references: Tipper station reference: standard and GLD operator stations are described as having two tippers per station.

steps.title: Open the Tipper model in the Sorter Sweeper Database
steps.purpose: Access the live configuration record for the operator station being investigated.
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), use the read-only view of the Sorter Sweeper Database and locate the Tipper model records for the relevant operator station.
steps.expected_result: The relevant Tipper model record or records are available for inspection in the Sorter Sweeper Database.
steps.healthy_condition: A Tipper model record is present for the identified station.
steps.failure_condition: The relevant Tipper model record cannot be located or is missing.

actions.label: Locate Tipper model records
actions.exact_action: Open the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only view of the Sorter Sweeper Database and locate the Tipper model records for the relevant operator station.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the relevant Tipper model record is missing.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The tipper model defines the tipper configuration used by the Sorter Sweeper system; the supplied source reference identifies Tipper ID, printer name with printer IP, location ID, and tipper status.

steps.title: Verify Tipper ID and station association

content.text: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API client (Apidog / WCS API) to (1) reopen any previously closed shoots/chutes and (2) cancel closeout exchanges that are not currently in progress. This is intended for recovery after a customer manual bag-out/closeout where the sort was not cycled.

steps.purpose: Use the service state as the observable indicator when logs are silent, matching the segment’s described behavior during crash periods.
steps.instruction: If the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) are Stopped (or show restart behavior), treat that as evidence consistent with the segment’s “service must stop” / “service was just like … gone” period during the suspected crash window.
steps.expected_result: Your conclusion matches the observed Status: Stopped/restarting supports the suspected crash/restart period; Running supports normal operation.
steps.healthy_condition: During normal operation, the OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) are Running.
steps.failure_condition: During the suspected crash window, the OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) are Stopped or restarting.

actions.label: Confirm evidence from service state
actions.exact_action: If the service is Stopped (or repeatedly restarting), treat this as evidence consistent with the segment’s “service must stop” / “service was just like … gone” period.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “except the service from the service must stop. Service must stop right… the log will be silent… you check the service services… there are 10 services.”

steps.title: Stop and escalate when service identification/status is unclear
steps.purpose: Ensure you do not proceed with an unsupported conclusion when the relevant service(s) cannot be identified or the status evidence is not clear.
steps.instruction: If you cannot identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) in the Services list, or if the Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status, stop and escalate.
steps.expected_result: Escalation is initiated with the evidence that the relevant service(s) could not be identified or status was unclear.
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant service(s) are identifiable and show clear Running/Stopped status.
steps.failure_condition: Service identification is ambiguous or the Services view does not provide clear Running/Stopped status.

actions.label: Escalate
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if you cannot identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) in the Services list or if the Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status.

Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “there are 10 services” and the segment’s stated challenge is knowing the service is gone when logs are silent by checking Windows Services.

success_criteria: You can identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) in the Windows Services MMC and observe clear Status values (Running vs Stopped).
During the suspected crash window, the observed service state (Stopped/restarting) aligns with the segment’s described “service must stop” / “logs may be silent” behavior.
healthy_conditions: OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) show Status = Running in the Windows Services MMC during normal operation.
failure_conditions: OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) show Status = Stopped during the suspected crash window.
OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) show restart behavior consistent with an unplanned crash/restart period.
Relevant service(s) cannot be identified among the ~10 services, or Running/Stopped status is unclear.
escalation_guidance: Escalate if you cannot map which of the ~10 services corresponds to the affected component or if the Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Transcript: “It’s a Windows… you check the service services… there are 10 services.” Also: “the service must stop” and logs may be silent.

missing_details: The segment does not name specific OptiSweep/WCS service names; the runbook therefore cannot provide a deterministic mapping from “affected component” to a specific service name beyond using the Services list to identify the relevant service(s).
